clue.text: Finest sort of shakedown

parts.note: read literally: shaking material through a mesh is a way of sorting out the finest particles, nothing to do with extortion or a makeshift bed

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: to sift is to shake flour or soil through a sieve, separating the smallest grains.

clue.text: Neither here nor there I have to describe some verbs thus

definitions.note: the clue asks for the adjective a grammarian applies to verbs that take no object

parts.note: someone in transit is on the way, at neither the start nor the destination
I have contracts to I've, written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A speaker with no fixed position has to explain how certain verbs behave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neither here nor there' usually means irrelevant; here it is taken literally, as being between two places.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term: verbs such as sleep or arrive, which take no direct object, are called intransitive.

clue.text: Variety theatre before end could have been placed in danger

indicators.note: Variety, as in a varied assortment, tells us the letters nearby are mixed into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A music hall could have been put at risk before the closing act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' suggests position but only joins the two words that 'Variety' mixes into one; 'could have been' leads to the definition. Variety theatre is the British name for vaudeville.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something threatened is put at risk or imperilled.

clue.text: Father has no hesitation accepting one belief

indicators.note: accepting says the shortened word takes a letter inside it
has no tells us the father loses the letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written
er is the sound of someone hesitating
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A priest unhesitatingly embraces a single creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a faith is a creed or religious conviction.

clue.text: City look after ducks

indicators.note: after places the word for look behind the ducks

parts.note: a duck is a cricket score of nought, written O, so several ducks are Os
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: In a city park, someone tends the ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look after' reads as one phrase meaning tend, but the two words split: 'look' gives letters and 'after' gives their position.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

clue.text: Remove Diane's ceremonial dress

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diane, and the possessive adds an S
a robe is a garment worn on formal or ceremonial occasions

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take off Diane's formal gown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as a loose description of the answer, since what is being removed is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: to disrobe is to take off one's clothes, so the verb means remove in the sense of undress.

clue.text: "Sanctioned" Kelvin found in dictionary

indicators.note: found in says the letter for Kelvin sits inside the dictionary's abbreviation

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: A man called Kelvin came across the word 'sanctioned' in a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to OK something is to approve it, so the past tense means approved or authorised.

clue.text: Coming from Aberdeen not dean reportedly at bank

indicators.note: Coming from says the answer is derived from what is left of the city's name, its letters put in a new order
not tells us the city's name loses the part that sounds like dean

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reportedly means dean is heard rather than read, giving the same sound in another spelling

parts.note: dean is pronounced like the last four letters of the Scottish city's name

explanation.surface: A man from Aberdeen, said not to be the dean, is standing at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns dean into DEEN, 'not' takes it from ABERDEEN leaving ABER, and 'Coming from' loosely signals rearranging those four letters. The definition is a Scots word, hence the Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots synonym: a brae is a hillside or steep slope, especially one running down to a river.

clue.text: Teacher went before contractor to psychiatrist

indicators.note: went before places the teacher ahead of the contractor

parts.note: a head is a head teacher, the British term for a school principal
whimsically, something that contracts, or gets smaller, is a shrinker

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher was ahead of a builder in the queue to see a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contractor' suggests a builder; here it is anything that contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: headshrinker, often shortened to shrink, is a jocular term for a doctor of the mind.

clue.text: Actor to begin but not finish

indicators.note: but not finish means the word for begin stops short of its last letter

parts.note: to begin is to start

explanation.surface: An actor is ready to start a job but will not see it through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not finish' removes the final T of START.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a star is a leading performer in a film or play.

clue.text: Flat-bottomed boat by crossing-place in town

indicators.note: by sets the boat next to the crossing-place

parts.note: a trow is a flat-bottomed sailing barge once used on the River Severn
a bridge is a place for crossing a river

explanation.surface: A punt is moored beside the ford in a riverside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Trowbridge is the county town of Wiltshire in south-west England.

clue.text: Reorder back-boiler

parts.note: the back of something is its rear
a range is a kitchen stove that often heats water too, as a back-boiler does

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rearrange things is to put them in a different sequence.

clue.text: I see a worm turn when it is tedious

indicators.note: turn tells us the letters of the four words before it are spun into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Watching a worm wriggle round soon becomes boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges I SEE A WORM; the surface plays on the proverb that even a worm will turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wearisome means tiring through dullness, or boring.

clue.text: In which one can buy nothing in particular?

definitions.text: In which one can buy nothing in particular?

parts.words: In which one can buy nothing in particular?
parts.note: a shop selling a bit of everything, whose name suggests it stocks nothing specific

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a general store sells all kinds of goods, general being the opposite of particular.

clue.text: Bill, he follows Peter with flamboyance

indicators.note: follows says the bill and he come after Peter's surname

parts.note: Peter Pan is J M Barrie's boy who never grew up
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC

explanation.surface: Bill trails along behind Peter in showy style.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: panache is dash, swagger or showy style.

clue.text: Rabbit having small cake before big apple!

indicators.note: before places the cake ahead of the city's abbreviation

parts.note: a bun is a small round cake
the Big Apple is New York, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: A rabbit eats a little cake and then a large apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bunny is the childish or pet name for the long-eared animal.

clue.text: One from Lyons, a pussyfoot, had longing as was not in a group

parts.note: un is the French for one, as spoken in the city of Lyons
pussyfoot is old slang for a teetotaller, abbreviated TT, after the prohibitionist Pussyfoot Johnson
to ache is to long for something, so had longing is ached

explanation.surface: A timid Frenchman from Lyons yearned for company, belonging to no group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pussyfoot' reads as a cautious person, but it is an old nickname for a teetotaller. 'as was' simply leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone unattached is independent, belonging to no body or partner.

clue.text: Washington state always environmentally friendly

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever faithful
green describes anything kind to the environment

explanation.surface: The state of Washington is forever kind to the environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname: Washington calls itself the Evergreen State, after its conifer forests.

clue.text: His share is the greater part

definitions.text: His share is the greater part

parts.words: His share is the greater part
parts.note: the proverbial biggest portion is named after this big cat, from Aesop's fable of the beasts dividing their kill

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the lion's share is the largest portion of anything divided.

clue.text: From the sea I returned to the river

indicators.note: From says the answer is taken out of the run of words that comes after it

explanation.surface: Someone came back from the coast to the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Aire is a Yorkshire waterway that flows through Leeds.

clue.text: An aptness developed along the way

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters of the two words before it growing into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A knack for doing the fitting thing grew as time went on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges AN APTNESS into a French phrase used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Translation: the French phrase en passant means in passing or by the way.

clue.text: Hurried up with speed to provide commentary

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom towards the top

parts.note: hurried means ran
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone dashed upstairs quickly to give a running commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to narrate is to tell a story or describe events as they unfold.

clue.text: Lady, one entering hostile land

indicators.note: entering puts the letter for one inside the disturbed land
hostile treatment is rough handling, so the letters of the word beside it are knocked about

parts.note: taken as written
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A lone woman crosses into enemy territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hostile' rearranges LAND to LNDA, and 'entering' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Linda is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Said Easterners had feeling of unease

indicators.note: Said tells us to speak the Easterners' name and listen for another word

parts.note: Malays are a people of Malaysia and the peninsula in south-east Asia

explanation.surface: People from the East reported that they felt uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: malaise is a vague sense of discomfort or disquiet.

clue.text: Gas coming from new boat first

indicators.note: first says the boat leads and the letter for new goes behind it

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Fumes drift from a brand-new boat at the head of the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: argon is an inert element found in the air.

clue.text: HP land?

definitions.meaning: HP is hire purchase, British instalment buying, nicknamed for payments that seem to go on for ever
the question mark hints at the imaginary island home of Peter Pan, a land that bears this name

explanation.definitionFit: Hire purchase is nicknamed the never-never in Britain, and Never Never Land is Peter Pan's island home.

clue.text: No exercises after Japanese drama

indicators.note: after puts the exercises behind the Japanese drama

parts.note: No, also spelt Noh, is the classical masked theatre of Japan
PE is physical education, the school lesson of exercises

explanation.surface: There will be no workouts once the Japanese play is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: nope is a casual way of refusing or denying.

clue.text: Urn placed against rough sea

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters of sea are tossed about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An urn is set down facing a stormy sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed' suggests a container but only links the definition to the wordplay; 'against' is the abbreviation seen in sports fixtures and court cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vase is an ornamental vessel, as an urn is.

clue.text: Some move erratically to change course

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people wander about unpredictably to alter their heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to veer is to swerve or turn suddenly onto a different heading.

clue.text: Poet named robin?

definitions.meaning: Thomas, the nineteenth-century English author of The Song of the Shirt, bore this surname
the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest called Robin bore this surname

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hood was a nineteenth-century English poet, and Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Definitely eastern European is attractive

definitions.note: a loose description: the clue wants a thing that attracts, namely the end of a magnet or cell that draws its opposite

parts.note: as a firm reply, definitely and positive both mean certain
a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: Without a doubt, the man from eastern Europe is good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attractive' suggests good looks; here it means exerting a physical pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose description: the positive terminal of a magnet or battery draws its negative opposite towards it.

clue.text: Food conference

definitions.meaning: what a person or animal habitually eats
a formal assembly or parliament, such as Japan's or the old imperial one held at Worms

explanation.definitionFit: A diet is the food one regularly eats, and also a legislative assembly or formal meeting.
